referenceSource.title: ICPC contest archive — Kattis judge index
referenceSource.scope: Third-party contest/problem metadata index; it states Kattis problem URLs use /problems/{id} and associates problem IDs with contest sources.
referenceSource.limitation: This index is not the official Kattis statement itself. A matching row confirms only the title/slug/contest metadata association, not statement contents, constraints, or long-scenario qualification.

gateDecision: Keep all 41 as candidate-only. Two additional official Waterloo source statements now corroborate candidate source claims (Cranes and Exact Change), but their exact Kattis slug crosswalks remain pending. Spiderman's Workout now has an institutionally hosted 2003 statement PDF, but its claimed championship provenance remains unresolved. Do not promote any record based on statement identity alone; verify canonical Kattis mapping and long-scenario qualification separately.

records.title: Exact Change
records.note: The official Waterloo 2008-10-04 contest page lists Problem C: Exact Change, and its linked original statement matches the candidate title and submitted contest/source claim. This corroborates the Waterloo source statement, but the exact Kattis `exactchange2` slug-to-source crosswalk remains unverified. Do not substitute `exactchange3`, which is a distinct problem.

alternateSourceConflict.contest: Archive index maps exactchange3 to PACNW 2024; it does not map exactchange2.
alternateSourceConflict.decision: The official Waterloo 2008 statement supports the candidate's claimed source, but it does not by itself establish the Kattis exactchange2 crosswalk. Retain the slug crosswalk hold; exactchange3 is a separate variant and must not be substituted.

statementEvidence.title: Waterloo ACM Programming Contest, October 4, 2008 — Problem C: Exact Change
statementEvidence.observation: For each case, choose bills/coins with total value at least the price, minimizing paid amount then number of bills/coins; price <=10000 cents and n <=100.

records.title: Cranes
records.note: The official Waterloo 2008-10-04 contest page lists Problem A: Cranes, and its linked original statement matches the candidate title and scenario. This corroborates the submitted contest/source claim. The consulted Kattis archive index still has no Cranes row, so the Kattis slug-to-source crosswalk and live Kattis page remain unverified. The Waterloo 2013 same-title statement is an alternate/reused copy, not the evidence used for this source match.

alternateSourceConflict.decision: Not used as source evidence. The claimed Waterloo 2008-10-04 source is now independently corroborated by the official Waterloo contest archive and Problem A statement.

statementEvidence.title: Waterloo ACM Programming Contest, October 4, 2008 — Problem A: Cranes
statementEvidence.observation: Square-grid candidate crane locations; each crane covers a radius-r disk; select a subset maximizing total covered area without crane interference; at most 15 candidate locations.
